text:
maria_support: customer on private VPC sees ALB target group go UNHEALTHY after DNS migration. app responds locally in pod, but ALB health check shows timeouts/5xx. they say nothing changed in SGs recently. can someone help triage?

sam_neteng: can you paste the healthcheck output from the target group + a dig from inside their VPC? also what protocol/port is the ALB health check using (HTTP/HTTPS) and any host override?

maria_support: copied outputs below. health check: 504 from ALB, "Target response failed". target group config: HTTPS:443, path `/healthz`, host override set to `app.customer.internal`. TTL for app.customer.internal was recently lowered to 60s. dig from a bastion inside VPC:```
;; ANSWER SECTION:
app.customer.internal. 60 IN A 10.2.4.18
```
curl from bastion (to the pod IP):```
$ curl -v https://app.customer.internal:443/healthz --resolve app.customer.internal:443:10.2.4.18
* Connected to app.customer.internal (10.2.4.18) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake start
* subject: CN=public.example.com
* issuer: Let's Encrypt Authority X3
> GET /healthz HTTP/1.1
> Host: app.customer.internal
< HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
```

lee_sre: that 400 on curl + CN=public.example.com indicates TLS SNI/Host mismatch. ALB HTTPS health checks do a TLS handshake and send the Host header/SNI you configured. if your backend expects SNI `public.example.com` but health check uses `app.customer.internal` (or vice versa) tls will fail or backend returns 400. also note ALB health check source ips are ephemeral, they come from the ALB nodes in the AZ — if you have an egress allowlist that only permits specific external IP ranges it can block health check responses if the backend does egress for auth.

sam_neteng: additional checks: 1) confirm listener -> target group is using TLS passthrough vs TLS termination. if your ingress (envoy) terminates TLS and expects a cert matching `public.example.com`, but ALB health check sends SNI `app.customer.internal`, envoy will reject. 2) look at envoy access logs around the healthcheck times (search for "GET /healthz" and source ip).

maria_support: fetched envoy logs for the timestamp range. snippets:```
[2026-03-15T12:03:21Z] "GET /healthz" 400 - "app.customer.internal" 10.2.4.18:443 -> -
[2026-03-15T12:04:21Z] "GET /healthz" 502 - "app.customer.internal" 10.2.4.18:443 -> -
```

toni_customer: FYI we did rotate certs and switched DNS yesterday to point to internal VIPs. we also tightened our egress allowlist to only allow outbound to a set of public IP ranges. we didn't change the ALB health check host though.

lee_sre: sounds like two simultaneous issues: TLS/Host mismatch from cert rotation + potential egress restrictions if your backend calls external auth providers during health check. quick repro steps to run in their VPC:```
# replicate ALB health check TLS handshake exactly
curl -v --resolve app.customer.internal:443:10.2.4.18 \
  -H "Host: app.customer.internal" \
  https://app.customer.internal:443/healthz
# inspect server cert
openssl s_client -connect 10.2.4.18:443 -servername app.customer.internal | openssl x509 -noout -subject -issuer
```
if the `-servername` SNI doesn't match the certificate CN/SAN you'll see handshake or 400 issues.

sam_neteng: mitigation options: 1) set ALB health check to use HTTP on port 80 (no TLS) and use Host header override if your app validates host; 2) update the health check host to the public cert name `public.example.com` so SNI matches; 3) provision a cert that includes `app.customer.internal` SAN; 4) ensure any outbound calls during /healthz are allowed by egress allowlist or stub them out for probes.

maria_support: customer tried switching the target group health check to HTTP:80 -> immediate green. they prefer HTTPS checks for prod. they asked: how do we make ALB HTTPS health checks send SNI `public.example.com`?

lee_sre: ALB health checks will use the Host header value you configure as the HTTP Host and will set SNI to that host when performing HTTPS health checks. so update the target group health check "Host" to `public.example.com` (not the internal name). and confirm envoy/ingress is set to accept that SNI. if you need path-based auth, consider a dedicated health endpoint that doesn't call external services.

toni_customer: updated host override to `public.example.com` and rotated the internal cert to include `app.customer.internal` SAN for long term. also relaxed the egress rule for our auth service IP for healthcheck windows. ALB now reports healthy. thanks. :tada:

k8s-bot: deploy status: health-check-change -> rollout complete to 3/3 pods (2026-03-15T12:25:13Z)

deploy-bot: note: we created a short-run canary for the cert change and health-check host fix, monitor for 15m for regression.

maria_support: closing thread, root cause: TLS SNI/Host header mismatch after cert/DNS change and restrictive egress allowlist. remediation: update target group Host override to match SNI expected by backend OR add SAN for the internal hostname + ensure egress to auth providers for health checks if necessary.
